advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have `check_cache_effective` distinguish an empty/too-short `usage_rows` input from a genuine 'ran but uncached' verdict (e.g. raise or return a distinct 'no-data' state).
evidence: `for i, row in enumerate(usage_rows): ... return {"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None}` — an empty list skips the loop and falls straight through to the False verdict.
The tests exercise only 2-row fixtures (test_check_cache_effective_marks_uncached_when_zero_reads / _marks_cached_on_later_hit); no empty-input case is covered.
Fail-open: the definite 'uncached' verdict is produced both when caching genuinely failed and when the check received no rows to inspect.
advisory.finding: `check_cache_effective` returns `{"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None}` for an empty `usage_rows` list (and for any single-row list), which is indistinguishable from the case where usage rows were never captured or the wrong input was passed. A caller folding this verdict into a report/ledger cannot tell 'ran and confirmed no caching' from 'no usage rows were ever collected'.
scenarios: A live run whose usage log failed to populate hands `[]` to `check_cache_effective`, which reports 'uncached' rather than 'no data'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or manage) the returned `config_root`'s cleanup responsibility so `resolve_pinned_model`'s temp dirs are not leaked across repeated calls.
evidence: `config_root = tempfile.mkdtemp()` followed by a `write_text` and `return PinnedModel(..., config_root=config_root)` — no `TemporaryDirectory`, no cleanup callback, no documented ownership contract for the returned path.
advisory.finding: `resolve_pinned_model` creates a temp directory with `tempfile.mkdtemp()` and returns its path but never registers cleanup, so every call leaks a directory (containing a `rebar.toml`) that persists for the process/system lifetime.
scenarios: Tier-1/Tier-2 eval callers invoke resolve_pinned_model per pass per run over a long-lived batch, accumulating orphaned temp dirs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either document that the caller owns deleting `config_root`, or expose a context-manager / register the dir for cleanup so it is reclaimed after the pass's LLMConfig is done.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch` treat a pass present on one side but absent on the other (or a missing `models` key) as a mismatch/error, not a silent pass.
evidence: `for pass_name in set(models_a) & set(models_b):`
`models_a = result_a.get("models", {})` — a missing `models` key yields an empty dict, so the intersection is empty and the loop body never runs (no raise).
This is a fail-open verification: the negative/absent result (no overlapping pass keys) is indistinguishable from the check having nothing to compare.
blocking.finding: `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch` compares only the INTERSECTION of the two results' model keys (`set(models_a) & set(models_b)`), so a result that is missing a pass entry — or is missing the `models` key entirely (defaulting to `{}`) — silently passes the diff-refusal. The guard cannot distinguish 'both sides stamped the same model' from 'one side never stamped its model at all', so a diff across a run where model stamping was skipped is admitted as if models matched.
scenarios: A report compares result_a (stamped pass1+pass2) with result_b that failed to stamp pass2 — the pass2 mismatch is invisible.
Either result predates stamping and has no `models` key: the diff is admitted with zero comparison.
